st.headline: Wilmar slides more than 4% after weaker Q3 earnings; Indonesian police probe plantation fires
st.teaser: Indonesian police are investigating about 28ha of plantation land belonging to Wilmar's subsidiaries.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Shares of agribusiness group Wilmar International tumbled more than 4% on Oct 29, extending a months-long decline as the company faced an Indonesian police investigation into plantation fires and reported weaker underlying third-quarter earnings.

The counter was trading at $3.12 as at 10.47am, down 4.6% or 15 cents from its previous closing price of $3.27. Some 4.7 million shares changed hands. This was the lowest the stock has been trading at since Jan 21.
The shares subsequently pared some losses to trade at $3.14 as at noon.
The sell-off on Oct 29 marked a further slide for Wilmar’s shares, which have shed more than 20% over the past six months. Shares of Wilmar were trading at $3.99 on Apr 8.

Wilmar revealed on Oct 28 , in response to queries from the Singapore Exchange Regulation, that Indonesian police were conducting preliminary investigations into fires affecting about 28 hectares of plantation land belonging to its subsidiaries in West Kalimantan.
The group said it was cooperating fully with the authorities .

According to Wilmar, its internal investigations found that the fires originated either outside its concession boundaries or in non-planted areas, including land farmed by local communities and conservation areas under its management.

The mainboard-listed company said it found no evidence linking the fires to its land preparation or clearing activities. It estimated losses involving crops and oil palms at less than US$500,000 ( S$640,000 ).

The disclosures came after the regulator issued a second round of queries to listed agribusinesses with operations in Indonesia, seeking further information on their exposure to the fires and haze affecting Singapore.

The regulator also asked companies to disclose any investigations by the authorities in Singapore, Indonesia or elsewhere, and whether they had links to 10 Indonesian companies issued preventive measure notices under Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
Wilmar said it had no operational, supply-chain or business relationships with those 10 companies.

Separately, Wilmar’s chairman and CEO Kuok Khoon Hong was among the company representatives who attended a closed-door meeting with Senior Minister K Shanmugam and other Singapore ministers on Oct 28 over the haze.

At the meeting, Shanmugam urged the companies to cooperate fully with investigations into the Indonesian fires, warning that the authorities would use their powers to establish responsibility for the transboundary haze.
Wilmar maintained that the fires and haze had not resulted in, and were not expected to result in, any material operational, financial, legal or regulatory impact on the group.
The developments came as Wilmar reported weaker underlying earnings for the third quarter ended Sept 30.

Although its net profit stood at US$281 million, reversing a year-ago loss that had been weighed down by a one-off compensation expense paid to the Indonesian government, its core net profit fell 25.2% year on year to US$267.3 million.
The group attributed the weaker underlying performance partly to higher raw material costs and lower soybean crushing margins. THE BUSINESS TIMES

cna.headline: Japan bonds steady ahead of BOJ decision; strong auction lends support
cna.teaser: Japan bonds steady ahead of BOJ decision; strong auction lends support
fullText: TOKYO, Oct 29 : Japanese government bonds (JGBs) were steady on Thursday, a day before the Bank of Japan's monetary policy decision, while strong demand at an auction of 2-year notes provided support.
The market was also buoyed by gains in US Treasuries after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged and gave few signals about the chances of a hike at the next meeting in December.
"The market seemed to perceive it as less hawkish than expected," said Yuhi Kawano, a market analyst at Mizuho Securities.
"Under these circumstances, it’s easy to see why the need for the Bank of Japan to raise rates at a high pace seems low, which should be supportive for the yen bond market."
• A measure of demand called the bid-to-cover ratio rose to 4.03 at the 2-year auction, from 3.89 at a sale last month
• The 10-year JGB yield also added 0.5 bp to 2.83 per cent, while the 5-year yield was flat at 2.265 per cent
• The 30-year yield edged up half a basis point to 3.88 per cent; the 20-year JGB hadn't traded as of 0514 GMT
• The BOJ is likely to leave rates unchanged on Friday and hike by a quarter-point in December, according to a Reuters poll of economists

listening.title: Singapore Expands Green EV Charging Network in Housing Estates
listening.transcript: Singapore is accelerating its transition toward cleaner transport by installing thousands of electric vehicle charging points across public housing estates. Officials report that over half of all HDB car parks now offer accessible charging slots for residents. This infrastructure expansion aims to support the nation's broader goal of phasing out internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040. Local drivers have welcomed the initiative, citing increased convenience and reduced range anxiety.

economistArticle.title: The Great Disconnect in Chinese Equities
paras: China’s industrial machine continues to churn out world-leading high-tech exports, from electric vehicles to solar panels, yet its domestic equity markets tell a starkly different story. Benchmark indices in Shanghai and Shenzhen remain sluggish, leaving local and international investors alike harboring a sense of profound gloom.

This paradox stems from a fundamental misalignment between corporate revenue growth and shareholder returns. While state-directed investment has propelled rapid technological advancement, intense domestic price wars and persistent deflationary pressures have severely compressed corporate profit margins across key manufacturing sectors.

Furthermore, real estate slumps have dampened consumer confidence, leading households to hoard cash in high-yielding savings accounts rather than risk their capital in volatile equity markets. Regulatory uncertainties and shifting policy priorities have further discouraged foreign institutional capital from taking long-term positions.

To reverse this skepticism, Beijing must demonstrate that policy interventions will focus not merely on supply-side expansion, but on bolstering consumer demand and safeguarding market transparency. Until investors see sustainable earnings growth translated into consistent dividend payouts, Chinese equities will likely remain a global anomaly.
economistArticle.cn:
中国的工业体系继续大量产出全球领先的高科技出口产品，从电动汽车到太阳能电池板不一而足，然而其国内股市却呈现出截然不同的景象。上海和深圳的基准指数依然低迷，使得本土与国际投资者普遍笼罩在一片深沉的消极情绪之中。

这种悖论源于企业收入增长与股东回报之间的根本不匹配。虽然国家主导的投资推动了技术的飞速进步，但国内激烈的价格战和持续的通货紧缩压力，严重压缩了各大关键制造业的企业利润率。

此外，房地产市场的低迷打击了消费者信心，导致家庭倾向于将资金囤积在收益相对较高的储蓄账户中，而非冒风险投向动荡不安的股市。监管政策的不确定性以及政策优先事项的动态调整，也进一步挫伤了外国机构资本长期建仓的积极性。

要扭转这种怀疑态度，北京方面必须表明其政策干预不仅关注供给侧的扩张，还将重点放在提振消费需求和保障市场透明度上。在投资者看到可持续的利润增长真正转化为稳定分红之前，中国股市很可能仍将是全球市场中的一个异常现象。

gems.s: While state-directed investment has propelled rapid technological advancement, intense domestic price wars and persistent deflationary pressures have severely compressed corporate profit margins across key manufacturing sectors.
gems.why: This sentence employs a contrasting clause starting with 'While' to skillfully balance positive macroeconomic achievements with underlying financial struggles. 本句使用 While 引导的让步状语从句，巧妙对比了宏观技术成就与微观财务困境，体现出极其严密的逻辑论述结构。
